rows.name: World 1-1 overworld scenery green (hill, bush, pipe, sky)
rows.notes:
Background palette 0 = [34,41,26,15] = [$22,$29,$1A,$0F] live on the first screen of World 1-1 (paused at level start, camera x=0, Mario on the hill). Proven slot by slot with write_palette + step_frame + screenshot, then clear_palette_overrides:
- slot 0 = $22 periwinkle = the SHARED BACKDROP (the sky). Writing it red painted the entire sky red. Every background palette's index-0 pixel renders this one color (PPU $3F00), so slots 0 of palettes 1-3 are dead registers.
- slot 1 = $29 lime green = the green bush on the right (nametable tile 54/chr 310) AND the warp-pipe body when a pipe is on screen; writing it magenta turned the bush pink while the hill stayed green.
- slot 2 = $1A green = the green hill the player stands on (nametable tile 52/chr 308) AND the pipe's shaded half; writing it magenta turned the hill pink while the bush stayed green.
- slot 3 = $0F black = the black outline/detail of the hill and bush (the hill's speckles/dots) and the pipe outline; writing it yellow put yellow marks on the hill.
So on this screen palette 0 = all the green outdoor scenery plus the sky.
rows.why: slot 1 written magenta turned the bush pink here, slot 2 turned the hill pink in 00d760f75272.png, slot 0 turned the sky red in b41a229e6644.png; roles as claimed (bush/pipe body, hill, outlines, backdrop)

rows.name: World 1-1 ground bricks (orange/tan brick floor)
rows.notes:
Background palette 1 = [15,54,23,15] = [$0F,$36,$17,$0F] live on the first screen of World 1-1. Used by the brick ground at the bottom (bottom ~2 rows, e.g. nametable tile 183 = chr 439). Proven slot by slot with write_palette + step_frame + screenshot:
- slot 0 = $0F black = UNUSED on this screen. Writing it red produced a pixel-identical frame: background palette index 0 always renders the shared backdrop (PPU $3F00 = palette 0 slot 0), so this register never shows.
- slot 1 = $36 peach = the brick's light top/highlight; writing it magenta turned the ground's light highlight pink.
- slot 2 = $17 brown = the brick BODY; writing it cyan turned the whole ground cyan/teal.
- slot 3 = $0F black = the brick outline / mortar lines between bricks; writing it yellow drew yellow outlines in the ground.
So on this screen palette 1 paints only the brick ground; nothing else here uses it.
rows.why: the ground's highlight is magenta after slot 1 was written; the claim's roles for palette 1 (highlight, brick body, mortar) match the ground row

rows.name: World 1-1 cloud + top HUD text (white)
rows.notes:
Background palette 2 = [15,48,33,15] = [$0F,$30,$21,$0F] live on the first screen of World 1-1. Shared, unusually, between the cloud and the fixed top status bar. Proven slot by slot with write_palette + step_frame + screenshot:
- slot 0 = $0F black = UNUSED (backdrop is shared; index 0 renders palette 0 slot 0).
- slot 1 = $30 white = the cloud's white body AND ALL the fixed HUD text/digits (MARIO, the 6-digit score, the x coin separator, WORLD 1-1, TIME and its digits). Writing it pink turned both the cloud and the whole top status bar pink.
- slot 2 = $21 sky blue = the cloud's shaded underside/rim; writing it red recolored only the cloud's shadow, HUD text untouched.
- slot 3 = $0F black = the cloud's black outline; writing it yellow gave the cloud a yellow rim.
Note the HUD text is NOT a separate palette: recoloring palette 2 slot 1 recolors every white letter and digit on the status bar.
rows.why: slot 1 written magenta turned both the cloud body and the HUD letters pink in this screenshot: palette 2 is shared by the cloud and the status bar, as claimed

rows.name: World 1-1 HUD coin / orange-brown blocks
rows.notes:
Background palette 3 = [15,39,23,15] = [$0F,$27,$17,$0F] live on the first screen of World 1-1. On this screen its only user is the small coin icon left of the coin count in the top status bar (nametable tile 46 = chr $12E; a background tile, with a behind-background sprite $FF hidden under it). Proven slot by slot with write_palette + step_frame + screenshot:
- slot 0 = $0F black = UNUSED (backdrop is shared; index 0 renders palette 0 slot 0).
- slot 1 = $27 orange = the coin's orange disc; writing it cyan turned the coin cyan.
- slot 2 = $17 brown = NOT VISIBLE on this screen. Writing it yellow produced a pixel-identical frame, and read_tile of the coin tile $12E shows it uses only pixel indices 0, 1 and 3 (no index 2). This slot is the ?-block bevel colour seen later in the level (the floating ? block also uses palette 3).
- slot 3 = $0F black = the coin's black outline; writing it yellow and sampling (92,24) gave $28 yellow, confirming index 3.
So palette 3 on the first screen = just the HUD coin (orange disc + black outline).
rows.why: slot 1 written cyan turned the HUD coin icon cyan here and nothing else on the screen; the claim says palette 3 paints only the coin icon on this first screen and later the ? block

rows.name: Goomba (walking enemy mushroom)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 walking enemy. PROOF: list_sprites (paused, game_mode $0770=1) decodes a 6-entry OAM group at slots 12-17, origin (184,185) that frame, all sprite palette 7 (OAM attr low bits = 3), no flips. Entries (tile id, x offset, y offset, flips):
- $FC (252), (+0,+0), none - blank top filler
- $FC (252), (+8,+0), none - blank top filler
- $70 (112), (+0,+8), none - upper-left (dome/head)
- $71 (113), (+8,+8), none - upper-right
- $72 (114), (+0,+16), none - lower-left (feet)
- $73 (115), (+8,+16), none - lower-right
The visible Goomba is the 2x2 body ($70-$73) at (184,193)-(199,208); the two $FC entries are its blank top row (the sprite form is 16x24). Sprite palette 7 live = [15,15,54,23] = [$0F,$0F,$36,$17] (slot1 black, slot2 peach, slot3 brown). Confirmed by hit-test: list_sprites at (156,197) returned OAM index 14 tile $70 palette 7, and get_pixel_color (156,197) = $17 brown = palette-7 slot 3. Found with no reference; palette 7 is shared with the invisible HUD coin sprite $FF.
rows.why: OAM $70-$73 in palette 7 under two $FC fillers; rendered from sprite CHR they are the Goomba's dome and feet, the Goomba at (184,193) in the screenshot

rows.name: Coin from a question block (flying coin)
rows.notes:
World 1-1 coin that pops out of a ? block when hit from below. PROOF: jumped into the first ? block (coin counters $075E and $07EE went 0->1), paused while the coin was in the air, and list_sprites decodes a 2-entry OAM group at slots 52-53, origin (102,85), both tile $61 (97) in sprite palette 6 (OAM attr low bits = 2):
- $61 (97), (+0,+0), no flips (attr $02) - upper half of the coin
- $61 (97), (+0,+8), flip_v (attr $82) - lower half, mirrored to close the oval
So it is an 8x16 vertical coin metasprite made of one tile used twice with a vertical mirror. Sprite palette 6 live = [15,22,48,39] = [$0F,$16,$30,$27] (slot1 red $16, slot2 white $30, slot3 orange $27); tile $61 uses index1 for the red center, index2 for the white bottom-left highlight and index3 for the orange edge. Confirmed by hit-test: list_sprites at (104,88) returned OAM index 52 tile $61 palette 6, get_pixel_color (104,88) = $27 orange = palette-6 slot 3. Found with no reference.
rows.why: the coin is in the air above the used block in this screenshot (coin count x01); OAM $61 twice, the second v-flipped, palette 6: $61 renders as half a coin, mirrored into the oval
